title: Towards Better Aligned LLM Judges for Radiology Report Evaluation across Modalities and Anatomies
abstract: arXiv:2604.03376v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Current work on radiology report evaluation has focused primarily on LLM-based metrics for chest X-rays (CXR), leaving open whether such approaches remain robust across other modalities and anatomies, and which model and prompt configurations are best suited to serve as LLM judges. We present a comprehensive evaluation of LLM judges for radiology report evaluation across diverse model families, prompting strategies, and adaptation methods, leveraging two expert-annotated datasets that span multiple imaging modalities and anatomical regions. Specifically, we compare four existing metrics (RadFact, GREEN, FineRadScore, and CRIMSON) with our proposed metric, VERT, across open- and closed-source models of varying sizes and reasoning capabilities. Among existing metrics, GREEN proves the most robust, outperforming more recent CXR-specific approaches. VERT further improves Kendall's correlation with radiologist judgment by up to 26% over G

translated_title: 迈向跨模态与跨解剖部位放射报告评估中更优对齐的LLM裁判
translated_abstract: 目前关于放射报告评估的研究主要集中在针对胸部X光（CXR）的基于LLM的指标上，这留下了两个悬而未决的问题：此类方法在其他成像模态和解剖部位上是否依然稳健，以及哪些模型和提示配置最适合作为LLM裁判。我们利用两个涵盖多种成像模态和解剖区域的专家标注数据集，对用于放射报告评估的LLM裁判进行了全面评估，涵盖多种模型家族、提示策略和适配方法。具体而言，我们将四种现有指标（RadFact、GREEN、FineRadScore和CRIMSON）与我们提出的指标VERT进行比较，测试对象涵盖不同规模和推理能力的开源与闭源模型。在现有指标中，GREEN被证明最为稳健，其表现优于更近期的CXR专用方法。而VERT进一步将与放射科医生判断的Kendall相关性相比G（原文在此处截断）提升了最多26%。
tldr: 该论文提出了一种新的放射报告评估指标VERT，并通过跨多种成像模态、解剖区域、模型家族及提示策略的全面评估，证明其与放射科医生判断的相关性相比现有最佳指标（如GREEN）可提升最多26%。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes VERT, a new radiology report evaluation metric, and through comprehensive evaluation across diverse imaging modalities, anatomies, model families, and prompting strategies, demonstrates that it improves Kendall's correlation with radiologist judgment by up to 26% over the best existing metrics such as GREEN.
